ques: Open the Credit Card Payoff Calculator, replace the defaults with a $5,000 balance, 22.5% APR, and $200 monthly payment, then report the payoff months, total interest, and final payment.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the credit card payoff calculator at the stated balance, APR, and payment. Report payoff months, total interest, and the final payment shown for that run. A different balance or payment fails.

ques: Use the Credit Card Payoff Calculator twice for a $3,600 balance at 19.9% APR: first with $150 monthly, then with $225 monthly. Compare the payoff time and total interest shown.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the credit card payoff calculator twice for the same balance and APR, once at each stated monthly payment. Bind each payment to its own payoff months and total interest. Swapping the two payments fails.

ques: Use the Student Loan Calculator for a $42,000 balance at 6.2% over 10 years with no extra payment, then change the extra monthly payment to $100. Report how many months and how much interest the extra payment saves.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the student loan calculator with and without the extra monthly payment. Report how many months and how much interest the extra payment saves versus the base term. The base term alone fails.

ques: Use the Savings Calculator with an $8,000 initial deposit, $350 monthly deposits, 12 years, and 4.25% APY. Report the final balance, deposits, and interest earned.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the savings calculator with the stated deposit, monthly amount, term, and APY. Report final balance, total deposits, and interest earned for that run.

ques: Use the Federal Income Tax Calculator for a married filer earning $145,000 with $12,000 in pre-tax 401(k) contributions and $20,000 itemized deductions. Report the deduction used, taxable income, federal tax, and displayed tax year.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the federal income tax calculator for the stated married filer, 401(k) contribution, and itemized amount. Report the deduction actually applied, taxable income, federal tax, and the tax year named on the calculator. Itemized input that loses to the standard deduction is not the deduction used.

ques: Use the State Income Tax Calculator for $110,000 of income as a single filer in Texas, Pennsylvania, and California. Compare the three estimates and state the limitation notice displayed by the calculator.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the state income tax calculator for the same single-filer income in Texas, Pennsylvania, and California. Bind each state to its own estimate and quote the calculator's limitation notice. Swapping states fails.

ques: Use the Paycheck Calculator for a single filer in Texas earning $92,000, paid biweekly, contributing 7% to a 401(k), with $2,400 annual pre-tax health premiums. Report net pay per period and annual take-home.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the paycheck calculator for the stated Texas single filer, salary, biweekly schedule, 401(k) percent, and health premium. Report net pay per paycheck and annual take-home.

ques: Use the Cost of Living Calculator to compare a $95,000 salary in Austin, TX with New York, NY, then reverse the cities without changing the salary. Report both equivalent salaries and explain what changes.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the cost-of-living calculator in both directions for the stated salary. Bind the New York equivalent to New York and the Austin equivalent to Austin, and explain what changes when the cities reverse. Swapping the two equivalents fails.

ques: Use the Mortgage Calculator for a $620,000 home, $124,000 down payment, 6.4% rate, 30-year term, 1.1% property tax, $1,800 annual insurance, and no HOA. Report monthly principal and interest and total monthly payment.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the mortgage calculator with the stated price, down payment, rate, term, tax, insurance, and HOA. Report monthly principal and interest separately from the total monthly payment. Swapping those two figures fails.

ques: Use the Retirement Calculator for age 41, retirement age 65, $105,000 income, $140,000 current savings, $1,250 monthly contribution, 6.5% return, 2.5% inflation, and 75% income replacement. Report the projected nest egg and whether the result says on track.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the retirement calculator with the stated ages, income, savings, contribution, return, inflation, and replacement rate, leaving other form fields at their displayed defaults. Report the projected nest egg and whether the result says the plan is on track. A conclusion that contradicts the displayed result fails.

ques: On the California financial advisor page, filter to Tax specialty and a maximum account minimum of $250,000. Report the result count and the first listed advisor's name, firm, rating, and minimum assets.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Open the California advisor list filtered to Tax and a maximum account minimum of $250,000. Report how many advisors match and the first advisor's name, firm, rating, and minimum assets. A different state's advisor fails.

ques: On the Florida financial advisor page, filter to Tax specialty and a maximum account minimum of $250,000. Report whether any advisors match and list the displayed advisor details if present.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Open the Florida advisor list filtered to Tax and a maximum account minimum of $250,000. Say whether anyone matches, and if so give that advisor's name, firm, rating, and minimum assets. An empty-result claim fails when a row is shown.

ques: Read the SmartReads article at /smartreads/how-the-standard-deduction-works. Report its author, reading time, and the distinction it gives between standard and itemized deductions.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Open the named standard-deduction SmartReads article. Report its author, reading time, and the distinction it draws between the standard deduction and itemizing. The same author on a different article fails.

ques: Read the SmartReads article at /smartreads/roth-ira-vs-traditional-ira-a-side-by-side-comparison. Report its author and summarize the stated tax-timing difference between the two IRA types.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Open the named Roth versus traditional IRA article. Report its author and the article's stated difference in tax timing between the two IRA types. Author alone, or the standard-deduction article's distinction, fails.

ques: Register a new account using a unique email, run the Credit Card Payoff Calculator with a $4,200 balance, 18.9% APR, and $175 monthly payment, save it as 'Changed payoff plan', then confirm it appears in Saved Calculations.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Register a new account, run the credit card payoff calculator at the stated inputs, and save it under the requested label. The saved row must belong to the new account and the answer must confirm that label. A pre-seeded account or a different payoff fails.

ques: Sign in at /login with alice.j@test.com and password TestPass123!, run the Savings Calculator with $12,000 initially, $500 monthly, 8 years, and 3.8% APY, save it as 'Eight year reserve', then report the saved summary from the account page.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Sign in as the stated user, run the savings calculator at the stated inputs, save it under the requested label, and report the summary shown for that saved row. A different label, user, or balance fails.

ques: Sign in at /login with bob.smith@test.com and password TestPass123!, calculate a $10,000 one-year CD at 4.5% APY and save it as 'CD deletion check'. Open Saved Calculations, remove that entry, log out, and verify that revisiting /account redirects to sign-in rather than restoring the session.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Sign in as the stated user, save the stated CD calculation under the requested label, then remove that entry. After logout, revisiting the account must land on sign-in. The entry still being stored, or a session that survives logout, fails.

ques: Use the Net Worth Calculator after changing cash to $9,500, savings to $28,000, brokerage to $47,000, retirement to $165,000, home value to $480,000, vehicles to $24,000, mortgage to $310,000, auto loans to $8,000, student loans to $12,000, and credit cards to $3,500. Report total assets, liabilities, and net worth.
judge_rubric: FACT CHECKPOINTS: Run the net worth calculator after changing only the fields the task names, leaving other asset and debt fields at their displayed defaults. Report total assets, total liabilities, and net worth. Zeroing an untouched default, or swapping assets and liabilities, fails.
